proposals.before: When Gao Yan ascended the throne, he concurrently served as Palace Aide to the Censor-in-Chief and became Inspector of Jiao Province.
proposals.after: When Gao Zhan ascended the throne, he concurrently served as Palace Aide to the Censor-in-Chief and became Inspector of Jiao Province.
proposals.reason: Chinese 世祖 is Northern Qi temple name Shizu for Gao Zhan (Wucheng), not Gao Yan (Xiaozhao / Suzong 肅宗).

proposals.reason: 身無擇行 means conduct with nothing open to censure, not 'no choice in personal conduct'.

proposals.before: At the end of Qi there were also Xin Ti of Longxi, merged-bureau director in the Masters of Writing, and Pan Ziyi of Changle, regular-attendant cavalier attendant—both known for talent and capacity.
proposals.after: At the end of Qi there were also Xin Que of Longxi, merged-bureau director in the Masters of Writing, and Pan Ziyi of Changle, regular-attendant cavalier attendant—both known for talent and capacity.
proposals.reason: 辛愨 is Xin Que (愨 què); the rendering Xin Ti misreads the given name.

decisions.reason: s0095’s 世祖踐祚 names Northern Qi Shizu (Gao Zhan / Wucheng), not Gao Yan (Xiaozhao / Suzong); replacing Gao Yan with Gao Zhan corrects the misidentification while leaving the offices intact.
The literal field likewise misreads 世祖 as Gao Yan; Gao Zhan is the correct personal name for temple-name Shizu in this Northern Qi context.

身無擇行 is the classical collocation for conduct with nothing open to censure, paired with 口無戲言; “no choice in personal conduct” is a false calque, and “irreproachable personal conduct” restores the sense.
Same mistranslation of 身無擇行 in the literal field; irreproachable personal conduct matches the Chinese and the parallel 口無戲言.
從兄 denotes an elder agnatic cousin, not a maternal-side cousin (表兄); dropping “by the mother’s side” removes invented kinship detail.

decisions.after: He left private life for a staff post under Grand Tutor Prince of Xianyang, then rose to secretariat gentleman.
decisions.reason: 太師咸陽王行參軍 is a staff post (行參軍) under the Grand Tutor Prince of Xianyang; 行 is not a personal name Xing. The proposed “Grand Tutor the Prince of Xianyang” is awkward, so the revised wording removes the false Xing without the intrusive article.

decisions.after: He doffed the headcloth and became a staff officer under Grand Tutor Prince of Xianyang, then was promoted to secretariat gentleman.
decisions.reason: Literal likewise mistook 行參軍 for a name Xing; the office is acting/staff aide under the Prince of Xianyang. Revised to drop Xing while avoiding the awkward “Grand Tutor the Prince.”
文林館 is Wenlin Hall; “Wenslin” is a typographical corruption of the same name, and the proposed Wenlin Hall matches 文林.
The literal field repeats the Wenslin corruption of 文林館; Wenlin Hall is the correct transcription.
Literal 從兄 likewise does not mean maternal cousin; removing “by the mother’s side” restores the kinship term without other changes.
文獻公 is the posthumous ducal title Wenxian, not a descriptive “Duke of Literature”; Duke Wenxian correctly preserves the title compound.
The literal field makes the same error on 文獻公; Duke Wenxian is the accurate rendering of the posthumous title.
文舉 romanizes as Wenju; “Wenzju” inserts a spurious z, and the proposed Wenju matches the given name while leaving the offices unchanged.

decisions.after: The Zhou court made him general of the establishment of the same rank and grand master of the Zai shi.
decisions.reason: 載師大夫 is the Northern Zhou Zai shi land-allotment grand master, not a carriage office; the proposal’s office sense is right, but title-casing the whole idiomatic sentence is awkward, so casing is kept in line with the original idiomatic style.
Literal Master of the Carriage Office misidentifies 載師; Grand Master of the Zai shi correctly names the Zhouli-derived land office in Northern Zhou nomenclature.
辛愨 is Xin Que (愨 què); “Xin Ti” misreads the given name, and Xin Que restores the correct personal name without changing the rest.
The literal field likewise mistransliterates 愨 as Ti; Xin Que is the accurate reading of 辛愨.
